verdict.rationale: Honeybadger has its own user-defined triggers. Alarms pair a BadgerQL query with a threshold and fire alerts, and users can choose which error events create a notification or ticket. A webhook integration with a bearer token can kick off external automations such as Cursor Automations, and deploys can auto-resolve open errors. However, the documented actions are limited to alerts, tickets, webhooks and deploy-triggered resolution, not a general rule-to-action engine. Missing for 10: a general-purpose rule builder with configurable actions beyond notifications/tickets/webhooks, detailed docs on rule conditions per integration, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Alarms combine a BadgerQL query (“count all slow requests in the past five minutes”) with a threshold (“when count is > 2”) and trigger alerts when the query result exceeds the threshold.
You get to choose which error events result in a notification or ticket being created
Our Webhook integration has a new bearer token field. Now, users can integrate Honeybadger with platforms like Cursor Automations.
By default, all unresolved errors are automatically marked as resolved when a deployment is recorded
